description: Python library for converting Python calculations into rendered latex.

Cover art by Joshua Hoiberg

handcalcs:
Python calculations,
as though you wrote them by hand.

`handcalcs` turns ordinary Python calculation code into a formatted calculation: the symbolic formula, then the formula with every value **substituted in**, then the result. Because the substitution step is shown, anyone can check the calculation by hand. The same calculation can go to different **renderers**: Markdown and LaTeX for Jupyter and documents, HTML for web pages, ASCII text for terminals and logs, a live, formula-based Excel worksheet and Word documents. You can restyle the built-in renderers or write your own. ## v2.0.0 Pre-release out now! This readme has been uodated to reflect the changes in handcalcs v2. As of 2026-11-06, the third release candidate is available for install: pip install "handcalcs==2.0.0rc3" or pip install --pre handcalcs **[Read the v2 documentation](https://handcalcs.structuralpython.com/)**: getting started, every renderer, a cookbook of recipes, and how to customize or write a renderer. ## Example ```python from math import sqrt # hc: -i ## Hypotenuse of a right triangle # Both sides are measured from the site drawings. a = 2.5 # Side a, in m b = 4.0 # Side b, in m c = sqrt(a**2 + b**2) ``` In Jupyter this is typeset as maths. With the ASCII renderer it reads: ```text ============================== Hypotenuse of a right triangle ============================== Both sides are measured from the site drawings. a = 2.5 (Side a, in m) b = 4 (Side b, in m) c = √(a² + b²) = √(2.5² + 4²) = 4.717 ``` ## Installing ```console pip install "handcalcs>=2.0.0rc3" ``` handcalcs 2.0 is a release candidate, so ask for it by version: a plain `pip install handcalcs` installs 1.x. handcalcs needs Python 3.11 or newer. Extras add the Excel and Word renderers (`handcalcs[excel]`, `handcalcs[word]`) and Jupyter export options (`handcalcs[exporters]`). See [Installation](https://handcalcs.structuralpython.com/getting-started/installation.html). ## Quick start In Jupyter, import handcalcs once, then start any cell with `%%render`: ```python import handcalcs ``` ```python %%render a = 2 b = 3 c = 2*a + b/3 ``` From a script, render a string or a `.py` file with any renderer: ```python import pathlib from handcalcs import HandCalcs from handcalcs.renderers import LatexRenderer latex = HandCalcs(LatexRenderer())(pathlib.Path("beam.py")) ``` On a function, `@handcalc(renderer)` returns the result and the rendered calculation. ## Renderers Markdown (the Jupyter default), LaTeX, HTML, ASCII text, a live formula-based Excel workbook, and Word documents with native equations. Subclass one to change its look, or write your own. See [Renderers](https://handcalcs.structuralpython.com/renderers/index.html). ## Upgrading from handcalcs 1.x handcalcs 2 is a rewrite around a parsed node tree and pluggable renderers. Most notebooks need only a few changes: `import handcalcs` instead of `import handcalcs.render`, and `# hc:` comment commands instead of `%%render` arguments. See [Coming from handcalcs v1](https://handcalcs.structuralpython.com/getting-started/migrating-from-v1.html). ## Gotchas Jupyter cells can run out of order. handcalcs looks up values in the notebook's namespace, so if you re-use variable names, a cell run out of order can render a **beautiful but completely incorrect** calculation. Run your notebook top to bottom before you rely on it. **If you use handcalcs for any kind of reporting that may become a legal document (e.g. design engineering calculations), it is up to YOU to ensure that the results are what you expect them to be. handcalcs is free and open-source software, and the author(s) are not responsible for incorrect calculations that result from its use.** That said, the whole point of showing the substitution is to make calculations easy to check by hand. ## YouTube tutorials These cover handcalcs 1.x; the ideas carry over. - [Getting Started with handcalcs (assumes zero Python knowledge)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZNFhLCWqA_g) - [Engineering Calculations: handcalcs-on-Jupyter vs. Excel](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=n9Uzy3Eb-XI) ## License Apache 2.0.
